function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity wasn’t “discovered” by a single person—it emerged from the work of many scientists over centuries. Here’s a quick overview:

| Era | Key Contributor | Contribution |
|-----|-----------------|--------------|
| **Ancient Greece** | Thales of Miletus (c. 600 BCE) | Noted that rubbing amber produced static charge. |
| **16th–17th century** | William Gilbert (1544–1603) | Published *De Magnete*, distinguishing magnetism from static electricity. |
| **18th century** | Benjamin Franklin (1706–1790) | Conducted kite experiments, coined terms like “positive” and “negative,” and proposed the single‑charge theory. |
| **Late 18th century** | Alessandro Volta (1745–1827) | Invented the voltaic pile (the first battery), demonstrating that electricity could be generated chemically. |
| **19th century** | Michael Faraday (1791–1867) | Discovered electromagnetic induction, laying groundwork for electric generators and motors. |
| **19th century** | James Clerk Maxwell (1831–1879) | Unified electricity and magnetism into Maxwell’s equations. |

So while no single individual “discovered” electricity, the cumulative work of these and many other scientists turned static observations into the modern science of electromagnetism.
